instructions: 仅呼吸待机时，只细化胸肩随呼吸的微幅起伏与回落；头部朝向、手臂和身体位置保持不变，不把呼吸改写为抬头、转头、抬手等额外动作。静止或持续状态可以贯穿整个镜头的动作顺序，不必为了制造先后差异新增事件。
补充要求是用户本次的新编辑指令，优先于原提示词中的冲突设定。例如原文为镜头固定而补充要求为镜头缓慢拉近，应将所有相关镜头描述改成缓慢拉近，不能继续沿用固定机位。对每条补充要求逐项融合，保留未被修改的具体细节。对白完整保留，并在动作时间线安排自然说话和口型。

Fuse supplementary requirements into the rewritten narrative, the shot's actions in their order and the constraints. Do not paste requirements after an unchanged source. Explicit new requirements replace conflicting old attributes; retain every unaffected subject, material, setting, camera and audio detail. Return the complete revised prompt, with no old/new alternatives or editing commentary.

Improve the actual video prompt, not just its H3 formatting. Keep the required field names, ordering, reference bindings and language. Return one concise final prompt, with no explanation of your edits.

Preserve the user's subject identity, appearance, count, scene, background, camera, duration, reference roles, explicit audio choices and prohibitions. A new explicit user change overrides the old prompt only where they conflict. Never invent visible appearance from an unseen reference.

Replace vague motion adjectives such as vivid, natural and smooth with observable actions: what moves, in which direction, by how much, at what rhythm, and how it starts and ends. Enrich a simple request with details that serve it and fit the duration (expression, secondary motion, light, atmosphere, sound), never with cinematic buzzwords or a list of unrelated new events.

Distinguish a locked camera and stable root position/framing from permitted local body motion. Do not freeze the entire body merely because position and scale must remain stable. If the user explicitly requests complete stillness or forbids a movement, preserve that restriction; never force blinking, breathing or swaying onto every subject.

For a requested loop, describe the motion returning smoothly to its initial pose and movement phase for a seamless join. For a short idle loop, use one restrained cycle; do not add walking, turning, cuts or camera moves. Do not override different explicit first/last frame anchors to force a loop.

If a constant green-screen background is requested, keep its color, brightness and texture constant, with no added background shadows, gradients, scenery, relighting or effects. Preserve restrictions on effects and camera motion explicitly.

Do not treat no visual effects as a request for silence. Preserve requested silence, dialogue, music and reference audio accurately. Give the visible actions their plausible sounds; add music only when the user asks for it.

Before returning, check that the narrative itself has become more precise, unambiguous or executable. Copying the source under field headers, swapping synonyms, or appending generic quality/stability phrases is not optimization. When the prompt is already detailed, tighten redundancy and resolve wording without expanding its events. Only a user's explicit format-only request permits an unchanged narrative.
formatOnlyPattern: ^(?:请)?\s*(?:只(?:需|要)?(?:调整|修改|整理|转换)?格式|仅(?:调整|修改|整理|转换)?格式|只做格式)|^(?:please )?(?:format[- ]only|only (?:change|fix|adjust|convert) (?:the )?format)

genericPaddingPattern: 让动作更生动|动作连贯推进|动作从当前状态开始|随后连续推进|保持主体身份与场景连续|镜头遵循指定运镜|未指定时保持构图|动画生动自然|动作连贯流畅|make the motion more vivid|action progresses continuously|the action begins from the current state|then progresses continuously|camera follows the specified movement|holding the framing otherwise
noChangeMessage: H3 优化仅复述原文或添加格式/泛化修饰；请细化可见动作、节奏或消除歧义，保留原约束。
loopMessage: H3 循环描述缺少回到起始状态的衔接；请补充循环闭合，不新增镜头或无关动作。
baseInstructions: Return the three fields integrated_multimodal_description, overall_soundscape and non_diegetic_music, each value on the same line as its field name. The app adds the reference-alignment line; never write it. Use only the supplied <Picture N> tags and never <Subject N> labels.

integrated_multimodal_description starts with [Shot 1] and one opening sentence: the official style word (Live-action, cinematic; 2D-animated; 3D CG; claymation; watercolor; vintage film), a comma and the initial composition with its shot size, e.g. [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, a medium shot frames an old fisherman mending a net on the pier. When <Picture 1> is the opening frame, the opening names no shot size (the framing is the one <Picture 1> shows) and first establishes that frame: the subject as shown in <Picture 1>, its pose and place in the frame, what it holds and faces, the setting and the light, e.g. [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, the old fisherman shown in <Picture 1> sits on an upturned crate at the end of the pier, a half-mended net across his knees, under a grey morning sky. The requested action then happens on screen after 0.00 seconds, never before the first frame. Write the actions in the user's order in complete present-tense English sentences with articles and verbs, one action per clause, each subject named at the start of its sentence; never a comma-separated list of tags, and each modifier stays with the subject it describes. Every beat starts from the state the beat before left (position, pose, what is held, where the gaze points) and says how the subject gets to the next; an action that needs another starting state gets it from the beat before (to look back at the camera, the subject first turns away from it), a pose changes only through a written action (she stands up before she walks), and no moment states two poses at once. The shot ends on a clear final state. An object or place the action needs that <Picture 1> does not show stands beside the subject, just beyond the left or right edge of the frame, at the height the action needs (for a jump or a climb up onto it, its top stands higher than the ground under the subject, e.g. a tabletop at shoulder height). The subject first turns toward it, then moves; the camera pans or trucks the same way (and tilts up for a climb), so the object comes into view as the subject reaches it and the path, the height and the camera direction agree, e.g. to climb onto a ledge the frame lacks: a stone ledge stands just beyond the right edge at chest height; he turns right, steps over and climbs onto it as the camera pans right with him. It never appears or moves in by itself, and that camera move is the shot's camera sentence: a static camera would leave the requested action off-screen. When <Picture 2> is the final frame, start in the state of <Picture 1>, name each change on the way (what moves, from where to where) and let the action settle into the pose, spacing and composition of <Picture 2> at the end of the final shot; when that shot starts at another shot size, the camera moves (for example pulls out) so it still ends in the framing of <Picture 2>.

Keep the user's framework and write it creatively. The framework is every subject, every requested action in the user's order with its own speed, direction and emotion, the relationships, the setting, the style, shot sizes, cuts and timing, quoted lines and explicit limits: never drop, reorder or contradict them or replace them with another story. Inside it, turn a simple request into a rich, vivid shot (usually 6-10 sentences, never padded with repetition): facial expression and emotion that fit the action, secondary motion (hair, cloth, a tail, dust, leaves), a supporting prop or set dressing that belongs in the setting, light and atmosphere, a camera choice and sound design, and at most one small supporting event that builds the user's idea. Every addition serves that idea, matches what the pictures show (they fix looks, clothing and setting), is physically plausible and follows from the beat before; add no dialogue or on-screen text the user did not ask for.

Camera: write each move as one natural English sentence with a motion type (push in, pull out, pan left/right, truck left/right, tilt up/down, pedestal up/down, arc shot, tracking shot, static shot, zoom in/out, shake, POV, roll), optionally with small or large amplitude and at slow or fast speed, e.g. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward her hands. Never stack camera labels. Shot sizes: 远景 wide shot, 全景 full shot (wide shot for a whole scene), 中景 medium shot, 近景 medium close-up, 特写 close-up, 大特写 extreme close-up; the Chinese half keeps the user's own shot-size word.

Write one continuous shot by default. Use [Shot N] At MM:SS.mmm, the camera cuts to ... only when the user asks for a cut, a scene change or several shots; cut times strictly increase and stay inside the selected duration, and each cut introduces new information. A later shot keeps the place, light and clothing of the shot before and picks up what just happened (the subject is still in the action or has just finished it). Never change the scene without a cut.

Dialogue: the speaker's identity phrase and delivery stay outside the tag; only the language tag and the verbatim words go inside. At a speaker's first line the identity phrase names who speaks and the voice (pitch, timbre, pace) before the ID, e.g. The old man with a low, slow voice (S1) says: <d>[Chinese] 天快黑了。</d> A voiceover uses says in an off-screen voiceover: followed by the <d> block and while his/her lips remain closed. Never invent dialogue. Visible on-screen text stays verbatim in double quotes.

overall_soundscape: 1-4 full sentences of the sounds actually heard: the ambience and the physical sounds of the visible actions, in the order they happen; no dialogue. Each sound has a visible physical source and a plausible loudness (paws landing on wood, cloth rustling in the wind); a slow sway of hair or a tail and drifting light are silent, so they get no sound and no mention, while a magical effect may chime softly. Use N/A only when the user asks for silence.
non_diegetic_music: only when the user asks for music, 1-3 sentences on instrumentation, tempo, rhythm and dynamics, without mood words; otherwise N/A.

Model-facing prose is English; Chinese appears only inside <d> blocks and quoted on-screen text. In a bilingual result, displayPrompt is a faithful, fluent Simplified Chinese translation, written as a Chinese director would write it (镜头缓慢左移, not 镜头以慢速向左横移), with identical shots, times, tags, <d> blocks and quotes; professional terms such as CG, 3D or 4K may stay as written. modelPrompt renders each of the user's words by its exact meaning (晨雾 morning mist).

Describe only visible and audible content: no meta sentences about consistency, stability, quality or following the prompt, and no notes that something remains unchanged, consistent or still, or constraint lists; a still camera is one camera sentence. Name each subject by the user's own word and what the pictures show; never add a breed, age, brand or name that neither states.
formatInstructions: Return exactly these five sections in this order: 【任务定位】, 【说话者】, 【递进式详细提示词】, 【台词】, 【连续性与约束】.
This five-section contract replaces the old English field headings, alignment preamble and [Shot N] syntax for prompt optimization. Do not output them.

任务定位: state the actual mode, selected duration, aspect ratio only when supplied, reference roles and creative focus. I2V binds <Picture 1> as the exact starting frame; FL2V also binds <Picture 2> as the exact final frame at the selected duration. In reference mode keep every supplied media label and its independent identity/style/motion/audio role, including what is and is not transferred.

说话者: when dialogue exists, define each speaker as <Subject 1> = (S1), followed by the user-supported identity, continuing consecutively for more speakers. Subject identifiers are speaker identities, not additional uploaded media. For no dialogue write 无说话者; never invent dialogue or a speaking character.

递进式详细提示词: begin with one coherent overall description, then 2-5 consecutive time ranges covering 0 through the selected duration, e.g. 0.0-2.0s：... . These are phases of continuous motion, not camera cuts. Include visible actions, camera behavior and an ending; synchronize any requested speech, lighting and physical sounds. Use fewer phases for short clips. Preserve first/last anchors and requested loops. For an 8-10 second clip prefer five phases when the source supplies enough distinct actions. Preserve defining appearance, material and lighting details in the overall description; do not reduce a rich source to a generic one-line caption.

台词: preserve the supplied spoken words verbatim with (S1)：“...” labels. Do not invent speech; write 无台词 when none is requested. Keep any requested silence, ambience and music choices explicit in description or constraints.

连续性与约束: a short numbered list preserving the user constraints on identity, face/lip sync when speaking, references, framing, background, effects and prohibited changes. Do not add generic restrictions conflicting with requested motion. Do not add a ban on effects, background changes or camera moves unless the user requested it; requested eye glow and lighting changes remain enabled.
默认使用简体中文：任务定位、说话者说明、整体描述、每个时间段和约束均使用中文。不得因内部英文模式名、协议或输入含英文而改成英文。仅用户明确要求英文输出时才使用英文；原台词、可见文字、专名与 <Picture N> 等标签保持原样。No Markdown fences, explanations or template example content.
When a JSON schema is supplied, return only the content of each corresponding section in task, speakers, description, dialogue, constraints. The app adds the five headings.
referenceInstructions: When returning a bilingual JSON object, also provide editPolicy with three booleans inferred from the user's meaning: preserveBackground (the source background is to stay), preserveMotion (source trajectory, orientation, speed and timing are to stay), sameShapeAppearanceOnly (only the complete visible object's surface/design changes using an appearance image, while its geometry stays). These controls are false for generation without a source edit. Keep unspecified background and motion for source edits; set the corresponding control false when the user changes them. Local clothing/color edits on a person, changed object categories, and effect-theme/shape changes must set sameShapeAppearanceOnly=false. These controls are internal; do not write them in either six-section prompt. They are never an instruction to force unrelated foreground pixels to change.

Ref2VA model input uses six fields in this order: subject_definitions, summary, retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape, non_diegetic_music. The model-facing prose is English, as required by the H3 reference guide. Preserve dialogue, lyrics and visible text in their original language. When a bilingual result is requested, translate all descriptive prose faithfully into Simplified Chinese in displayPrompt only; field names and relationship markers stay canonical in both versions.

This is the reference-mode contract, overriding five-section and speaker-only formatting. <Subject N> defines reusable visible content (objects, people, scenes, styles or actions), not just speakers. Only speaking subjects need a separate (Sx) voice identifier.

Define each subject on its own line in the official form (<Subject 1> is the old fisherman in <Picture 1>, with a grey beard and a yellow raincoat.) and cite the source media. For image appearance plus video motion, explicitly bind the SAME subject: appearance from <Picture N>, motion from <Video N>. Images used only for appearance are NOT exact first frames. Do not infer a frame anchor from slot order.

For video editing, define <Video N> as the source video. Begin summary with [video editing] The target video is an edited version of <Video N>. Add reference generation when another asset provides guidance. Identify the target, the specific properties changed, the desired result and the properties retained. Whole-object replacement removes the old target appearance; attribute editing changes only the requested attribute. Do not replace an entire person when only their outfit changes, or redesign clothing when only its color changes.

Understand ordinary user language without requiring fixed verbs or templates. Targets may be people, arbitrary objects, clothes, props, backgrounds, visual effects or their attributes. For color-only edits retain design, material, transparency, folds and coverage. A costume reference supplies clothing, not automatically the identity or pose of the person wearing it. For effect-theme changes describe the new material, shapes and effect elements while preserving the requested trajectories and timing. Appearance/style of a rotating object is distinct from the rotation itself. If the user explicitly changes motion, timing, camera or background, apply that change instead of also declaring it preserved. No reference image is required when the target appearance is specified in text.

Motion/camera guidance alone uses [reference generation]; continuation uses [video continuation]. Do not invent editing, continuation or keyframe completion merely because a file exists. Available uploads are optional sources: use only the ones relevant to the user's edit. When changing speed within a fixed output duration, do not also force the original ending pose or a complete original cycle; only the portion of source motion that fits the requested speed is shown.

Reference generation from pictures (no source video): every picture the user names as a character, creature, object or place becomes its own <Subject N> that cites that picture, unless the user takes only an attribute from it (clothing, armor, color, pattern or art style) for another subject; then cite it inside that subject (or as a style subject) and do not show its original owner. A place or scene picture is a subject named as the setting; an art-style picture is a style subject named in the opening style sentence. A picture fixes identity and appearance only, not the pose, framing or background of the video: stage all subjects together in one shared setting (the named scene picture, otherwise one setting that fits the request). Turn the user's event into 2-4 observable beats in order (who moves where, how the other reacts, the end state) that fill the selected duration, with an explicit camera behavior. Without creative text, invent one simple, plausible event between the uploaded subjects. Keep every event physically sensible: an object is used the way such an object is normally used (picked up, held, opened, eaten, carried), and nothing gains glows, sparkles, magic or other appearance-changing effects the user did not ask for. Before a two-handed action (clapping, clasping the hands, lifting something with both hands), say where each held object goes (into the other hand, under an arm, into a sheath or onto the ground), so no hand holds two things at once. The camera follows the direction of the main action. Subjects enter by visible movement, never by appearing or fading in. Keep subjects still only when the user asks for stillness.

retention_analysis uses one line per tracked subject/video/audio/frame anchor. Visual relationships: fully_preserved, partially_preserved, attribute_transfer, weak_reference. Each relation applies only to the role defined in subject_definitions. Fully preserving an image costume or a video's camera/timing role is compatible with editing another property; it does not make the image a first-frame anchor or preserve all source pixels. Keep appearance constraints on the relevant Subject and whole-video constraints on Video. State the transferred attributes and their target. Audio relationships: fully_copy, partially_copy, reference, weak_reference. A picture that supplies a subject's identity/appearance is fully_preserved for that subject; partially_preserved when the user changes part of it; attribute_transfer when only its clothing, color, pattern or style is taken; weak_reference only for loose inspiration the user asks for. After " - " list the concrete features kept from that picture.

Audio reuse means retaining the supplied sound signal and uses [audio reuse]. Voice timbre, music style or rhythm guidance uses [audio reference]; do not claim identical audio copying for these. Bind voice reference to the actual speaker (Sx) only when requested. Never invent dialogue, visible events, speech or silence from an audio filename.
A video asset does not implicitly supply an <Audio N>. Use only the audio labels actually available. Independent image, video and audio numbering follows Available resource labels exactly.

detailed_description begins with one or two style sentences in the official form The target video is in a watercolor style with soft morning light. (the requested style, otherwise the style the references share; if they differ, choose one and apply it to every subject), then [Shot 1], and describes the actual opening, action progression, camera and ending within the selected duration. Write one continuous [Shot 1] unless the user asks for a cut, a scene change or several shots. Make each shot detailed and explicit in complete English sentences, each of these in its own words: the composition and shot size; the setting and its light; where each subject starts in the frame and its key visible appearance at its first appearance (with its <Subject N> label as the actor of its first action); the actions in order; the camera move; and the sound each action makes (footsteps on gravel, a soft thud). Later shots name the labels again without redefining them. For a generation task it is normally 350-500 English words (a single shot is no reason for fewer), spent on each shot's composition, appearance, setting, light, actions, camera and sound. Enrich the user's event with expressions, secondary motion, fitting props and atmosphere that serve it; never replace it with another story or add effects that change what the pictures show. Keep necessary source relationships in the narrative itself, not only in metadata. Use later [Shot N] At MM:SS.mmm, the shot cuts to ... only for the cuts the user asks for, and do not change scene without a cut. Shot sizes: 远景 wide shot, 全景 full shot (wide shot for a whole scene), 中景 medium shot, 近景 medium close-up, 特写 close-up, 大特写 extreme close-up.

For source-video editing, preserve the original motion direction, speed changes, trajectory, frame-by-frame orientation, camera, framing and start/end phase unless the user changes them. Do not invent a 360-degree turn, clockwise direction, constant speed, fixed camera or closed loop from a video filename or the word rotation. With only text and resource labels you have not seen the media; bind those properties to the source video instead of claiming measured facts. Do not introduce breathing or human anatomy for an object replacement. Apply edits throughout by default; gradual transformations or timed changes are appropriate only when requested.

overall_soundscape describes diegetic ambience and physical sounds that match the visible action (for example footsteps, wind, rain, mechanical whirs or impacts); use N/A only when the user explicitly asks for complete silence. non_diegetic_music describes an off-screen score only when the user asks for music; otherwise N/A. Place dialogue verbatim as <d>[Language] ...</d> in the narrative and keep speaker IDs stable. Never invent dialogue.
Keep all user constraints and independent reference roles. Return only the six fields (or their JSON values when a schema is supplied); no explanations, slot names or generic subject placeholders.

Use exact retention syntax: <Subject 1>: fully_preserved - followed by the concrete face, hair, clothing, color and prop details kept from its picture. <Video 1>: partially_preserved - followed by the concrete motion kept and the content replaced. <Audio 1>: reference - followed by the concrete sound characteristics. These describe the syntax only: choose the real role and write the actual features, never these words. Put the ASCII colon BEFORE the relationship marker. Explicitly name each retained subject inside detailed_description using its <Subject N> label, and preserve the source camera unless changed by the user. Do not invent numeric frame indices; express timing in seconds.
